AT-02.reason: Eastern Austria combines Alpine margins with the Vienna Basin and eastern lowlands.

CH-01.reason: The Swiss Plateau territory includes upland margins but is not predominantly Alpine terrain.

CY-01.reason: Cyprus combines coastal plains with the Troodos and Kyrenia uplands.

DK-01.reason: Jutland is predominantly low and readily traversable.

DK-02.reason: The Danish islands are predominantly low and highly connected.

FI-01.reason: Southern Finland mixes low relief, forests and lakes.

FI-02.reason: Central Finland is dominated by forests, lakes and moderate relief rather than named mountain regions.

GB-02.reason: Northern England combines urban lowlands with Pennine uplands.

GB-04.reason: Southern England is mainly accessible lowland with local uplands.

GB-06.reason: Northern Ireland combines rolling lowlands and modest uplands.

GR-03.reason: Crete and the larger Aegean islands are rugged despite their maritime climate.

IE-01.reason: Western Ireland combines rough coastal uplands with central and river lowlands.

IE-02.reason: Eastern Ireland and Dublin are predominantly accessible rolling lowland.

IT-03.reason: Southern Italy contains major Apennine and Calabrian barriers but also substantial coastal and agricultural lowlands.

IT-04.reason: Sicily combines mountain massifs with broad coastal and interior agricultural areas.

IT-05.reason: Sardinia is rugged but contains traversable plains and plateaux.

MT-01.reason: Malta is low and compact, with broken limestone relief rather than major mountains.

PL-04.reason: Southern Poland and Silesia include the Carpathian and Sudeten edges alongside dense basins and lowlands.

RO-02.reason: Wallachia combines the Southern Carpathian edge with the broad Romanian Plain.

RU-02.reason: Northwest Russia includes Karelia, Murmansk and Arkhangelsk as well as the St Petersburg corridor.

SE-01.reason: Southern Sweden is mainly low and well connected, with forests and local uplands.

SE-02.reason: Central Sweden combines lake country, forest and urban lowland.

TR-01.reason: Eastern Thrace and Istanbul combine rolling terrain with dense urban and transport corridors.

UA-05.reason: Crimea combines northern steppe with the mountainous southern coast.
